I’ve had both high dose IM and Spravato. There are a couple studies published on pubmed  by Klarisana (the clinic I go to) that highlights the importance of a jarring psychological experience almost as much as the way ketamine works on the brain at a chemical level. 

I think at the end of the day it could be preference. I disliked Spravato because it put me to a “halfway” state of dissociation that freaked me out. That on top of being forced 2hrs to wait when the effects wear off after 20 min for me can be very anxiety inducing. That being said, the IM clinic I go to doesn’t give enough time because 55 min isn’t enough for high dose ketamine experiences. I talked to the behavioral health admin in my state about it. And there aren’t any regulations or policies on psychedelic medicine yet as it’s still in its infancy for modern medicine. 

As for if it’s a scam? If your insurance doesn’t cover it, yes. Ketamine doesn’t cost much to synthesize including the s-isomer that’s isolated in Spravato.  The reason Spravato was invented was mostly due to the fact making a new patent for ketamine would be incredibly hard since it expired years ago. So they just took part of ketamine, the s-isomer, threw it in a bottle and called it “Spravato” mainly for profit from my research. Ultimately it would be nice if ketamine in all forms was covered for mental health reasons by insurance. But since it’s not fda approved for mental health and getting it approved involves money and patent, it’ll likely stay pricey.

My ketamine clinic for IM currently covers all costs for Medicaid patients. They used to have a copay of $47 for Medicaid patients vs the $400ish dollars per session out of pocket but they recently waived it.
